title: SSE: invalid-byte drain discards buffered valid UTF-8 data
description: client.rs subscribe_events: When raw_buf starts with invalid UTF-8, drain_end = valid_up_to.max(1) removes only ONE byte from the invalid-sequence head. If the invalid bytes span multiple bytes (e.g. a lone 0xC2 followed by 0xFF 0xFE ...), subsequent calls decode the same partial sequence repeatedly before eventually reaching valid data. Each iteration valid_up_to==0 so we drain only 1 byte, burning through invalid bytes one at a time. This is correct for progress, but each loop iteration triggers the cap check on raw_buf without any useful decode — a carefully crafted stream of invalid bytes interleaved with valid ones can cause the 1 MiB raw_buf cap to fire even when the actual UTF-8 content is small. Result: spurious SseFrameTooLarge error on a stream that has valid content preceded by <1 MiB of garbage bytes. Not a correctness bug per se for the common case; the cap exists for protection. But the drain-one-byte strategy combined with the cap check on the UNDRAINED buffer (before we shrink it) means the actual limit is raw_buf.len() >= 1 MiB, not decoded content >= 1 MiB. A 1 MiB run of single invalid bytes each followed by a delimiter will kill the stream even though no frame exceeds a few hundred bytes.
